status: provisional constrained engagement candidate, not a production joint reconstruction

sources.reviewed: Factory image identifies the separate forked drive lever, drive assembly, plunger-side connection, housing seal and solenoid. It does not dimension the linkage or establish this candidate's slot, spherical pads, groove or pivot geometry.
Conventional prior-art discussion supports plunger-actuated engagement and spring-biased return. No production adoption or 1994 linkage dimensions inferred.

kinematics.accommodation: Upper pin slides transversely within the translating plunger clevis. Lower spherical pads slide laterally within an annular clutch groove while retaining axial contact. This is a provisional rigid linkage, not a production-construction claim.
kinematics.return: Prescribed fraction can reverse to zero and restores every replacement shape. Spring return force, friction and tooth-blocking are not solved.

interfaces: Housing fork passage widened to51mm with upper surface atz=-1.5;25mm radial clearance stops there to retain nose-bar attachment.
Clutch collar clearance21.2mm radius ends atz=1; original shaft/pinion front clearance remains.
Seal slot enlarged around the rotating stem; no elastomer deformation or sealing rating modeled.
Solenoid front seat bore enlarged to13mm radius for the stem's final-stroke envelope.

integration.api: Use starter_engagement.api(base3) beneath both existing explanation and solenoid geometry adapters. Keep root-owned solenoid explosion metadata wrapper in place.
integration.parts: Eight replacement definitions, no new occurrences. Default static/retracted pose.
integration.motion: parts(fraction,baseline) returns replacement shapes; switch.parts(fraction) supplies coordinated spring/contact shapes. This does not install a running-starter viewer animation.

limits: Fork pads and clevis slot are provisional, not recovered Ford production details.
No force, wear, tolerance-stack, thermal, electromagnetic or tooth-blocking simulation.
Existing manual flywheel mounting and tooth-profile assumptions remain unchanged.
Overrunning clutch internals and electrical lead connections remain unresolved.
